changes.finding: C04 F1: pipe fixture versus PTY Spawn transfer
changes.before: Constructs requests with three pipes, explicit environment and 1500 ms grace; bounded block() runs futures on a caller runtime separate from the library runtime.
changes.after: The Mode::Pipe fixture uses three stdio pipes; its Mode::Pty variant sends no child stdio descriptors or handles with Spawn. Both use explicit environment and 1500 ms grace; bounded block() runs futures on a caller runtime separate from the library runtime.
changes.reason: spec selects Mode::Pipe or Mode::Pty while retaining the explicit environment and grace. spawn_on creates three stdio pipes only for this unmerged piped-input fixture; its PTY branch has zero child stdio handles and an empty descriptor vector. The Unix helper asserts zero received descriptors for PTY.

changes.finding: C04 F2a: drive-relative command and NUL validation categories
changes.before: InvalidArgument covers empty command, NUL fields, malformed env keys, drive-relative paths, PTY sides and numeric ranges.
changes.after: InvalidArgument covers empty command, NUL fields (including nul_in_cwd), malformed env keys, drive_relative_command, PTY sides and numeric ranges.
changes.reason: drive_relative_command uses invalid(), which constructs InvalidArgument. nul_in_cwd also goes through nul() and invalid(); it must not be grouped with the distinct drive_relative_cwd constructor.

changes.finding: C04 F2b: residual lookup failure and cwd resolution/access categories
changes.before: NotExecutable distinguishes directory, permission and unsupported Windows extension; filesystem lookup failures become Io and cwd failures InvalidCwd.
changes.after: NotExecutable distinguishes directory, permission and unsupported Windows extension. lookup_failed returns Io for residual filesystem errors, apart from separately classified missing and permission cases; drive_relative_cwd and cwd resolution/access failures return InvalidCwd, while nul_in_cwd remains InvalidArgument.
changes.reason: lookup_failed constructs Io for residual filesystem errors. Resolution separately skips missing/non-directory candidates and classifies permission refusal. drive_relative_cwd and the cwd resolution/access constructors use bad_cwd(), which constructs InvalidCwd; the earlier NUL validation remains InvalidArgument.

changes.finding: C04 F3: initial Go failure versus later exited query
changes.before: Resize after observed exit is Closed; failed terminal exec produces Io because no exit status exists.
changes.after: Resize after observed exit is Closed. For a held Unix terminal, Go preserves the translated SpawnFailed code (NotFound in the supplied test); a subsequent exited() query reports Io, using terminal_never_started while the generation remains alive because no exit status exists.
changes.reason: Tree::go maps a GoEnd::Failed through failed(), retaining the translated SpawnFailed code. The failed Go marks life gone/lost without creating an exit status. exited() then uses lost(); with a live generation this is terminal_never_started/Io. The test explicitly requires initial NotFound and subsequent Io while the generation remains alive.

changes.before: spawn/validate.rs and spawn/resolve.rs enforce these checks.
changes.after: spawn/validate.rs owns the verbatim option and resolved-target checks, orchestrated by spawn::prepare; spawn/resolve.rs supplies the resolved executable path.
changes.reason: validate::check owns option/platform/argv/NUL checks; validate::verbatim_program owns batch-target refusal. prepare invokes validation before resolution and resolved-target validation afterward. resolve::program supplies the resolved path.
